proposals.evidence: DEDR 5151 directly documents the corresponding who forms: Brahui dēr, Gondi bor, Kannada yār, Kodagu/Kota dār, Kurukh nē, Malayalam ār, Malto né, Parji ēd, Tamil yār, Telugu evaru, Toda ōry and Tulu ērů. Source cognacy explicitly identifies this article. Final vowels and Malto -du are retained as surveyed morphological variants, not removed. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 600 explicitly groups Gondi/Kota/Gadaba un-/uṇ- drink, Kurukh ōnnā and Malto óne/onde. The survey cognacy annotations point to this family; full article checking supports the same drinking verb. Kota unatukə and Malto hōnā remain intact as inflected/transcribed survey responses, with no silent truncation or normalization. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 4885 directly groups the mīn fish series in Kannada, Kodagu, Kota, Tamil, Tulu and Malto (mínu). The survey final -ə and Malto -du are retained. Badaga and Ravula are comparative extensions explicitly labelled look-alikes by the upstream annotation; neither is falsely described as listed in DEDR. The article’s Sanskrit mīna comparison does not itself specify a loan route for these records. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 5401 gives Kolami vitanam, Kota vit, Malayalam vittu/vita/vitar, Parji vittid, Tamil vitai, Telugu vittanamu and Toda pït in the seed/sowing family. Source annotations independently identify the article. Survey Tamil vedə and Toda pittə remain comparative spelling/ending variants. The possible Indo-Aryan bīj-/bic- seed responses are excluded from this proposal. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
